reading: The grid is cut into panels by full separator lines. One panel holds a template shape; the first panel of each panel-row holds a colour block. Every panel of a row becomes the template shape painted in that row's colour.
verb: stamp template per panel in row colour

slots.panels: cells cut by the full separator rows/columns
slots.template: the shape in the one panel that differs from the colour blocks
slots.colour: the colour of the block in the first panel of each panel-row
slots.result: every panel of that row = template recoloured to that colour; separators kept

why: every non-separator panel equals the template mask in its row's colour

reading: Panels come in left/right pairs separated by background lines; each panel has its own background colour and a shape. Each panel gets its partner's shape (same relative position), painted in the partner's background colour, on its own background.

slots.pair: two panels on the same panel-row, split by the 0 separator
slots.shape: the cells of a panel that differ from its background
slots.result: panel P = bg(P) everywhere, except cells where partner Q has shape, which become bg(Q)

why: out(P)[y][x] = bg(Q) if in(Q)[y][x] != bg(Q) else bg(P), for each paired panel P,Q

reading: One large shape is a 3x3 pattern scaled up by a block factor, among scattered noise cells of another colour. The output is the 3x3 pattern downscaled, with filled blocks painted in the noise colour.

slots.shape: the largest object (blocky, 3x3 blocks of size k)
slots.noise colour: the colour of the scattered single cells
slots.result: 3x3 grid: block filled -> noise colour, else 0

why: each output cell = noise colour iff the corresponding k x k block of the large shape's box is filled

reading: Two-cell key pairs at the left edge map shape colours a -> b. Each shape gets a box of colour key(a): every background cell in its bounding box grown by one, except enclosed holes, becomes key(a).
verb: frame each shape in key colour

slots.key: 2-cell components of two colours a,b on the left edge
slots.subject: each object of colour a
slots.region: background cells in the object's bounding box expanded by 1, excluding holes enclosed by the object

why: every non-enclosed bg cell within bbox+1 of an object of colour a becomes key(a); nothing else changes

reading: The 4x4 input is tiled 4x4 into a 16x16 grid: a copy of the input goes in each block whose corresponding input cell is non-background; other blocks are empty.
why: block (i,j) is the input iff input[i][j] is fg, else empty

reading: There is a 2x2 square of colour 1 and one of colour 2. The 1-square shoots a diagonal line of 1 up-left from its top-left corner, the 2-square shoots a diagonal of 2 down-right from its bottom-right corner, each to the grid border.
why: each line reaches the border; direction is fixed by colour (1: up-left, 2: down-right)

reading: Three markers lie on a diagonal at equal spacing d. Concentric square outlines of the marker colour are drawn around the middle marker with radii d, 2d, 3d, ... until they leave the grid.

slots.centre: the middle of the three markers
slots.step: the diagonal spacing d between markers
slots.result: square rings at Chebyshev distance k*d from the centre, clipped to the grid

why: a cell is coloured iff its Chebyshev distance to the centre is a multiple of d (including the centre)

reading: The input is three 5-wide panels split by separator columns of 6. The output 5x5 is spliced: columns 0-1 from the first panel, column 2 from the second, columns 3-4 from the third.

slots.panels: the three stripes cut by full separator columns
slots.result: output column j taken from panel A for j<2, panel B for j=2, panel C for j>2 (same column index within the panel)

why: out[y][j] = panel_k[y][j] with k = A,A,B,C,C for j = 0..4

reading: A single marker shoots diagonal lines of its own colour in all four diagonal directions to the grid border.
why: the four diagonal rays from the marker reach the border

reading: A shape of 8s is partitioned into 2x2 squares and L-trominoes (2x2 minus one cell). Squares become 1; L-pieces are coloured by which corner is missing: top-left missing -> 2, bottom-left missing -> 3, top-right missing -> 4.
verb: tile into pieces and colour by piece type

slots.subject: the 8-coloured cells
slots.pieces: partition into 2x2 squares and 3-cell L shapes within 2x2 boxes
slots.colour: 1 for square; 2/3/4 for L by missing corner (TL/BL/TR)

why: every 8 cell is recoloured by the piece it belongs to; background unchanged
